result.title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents
result.summary: AI agents can write programs that carry out a task without calling a model at every step, so the task runs fast and its logic stays open to inspection. Agents improve these programs by running them, studying their failures, and revising the code, a form of recursive self-improvement (RSI). We ask whether this process also yields runtime checks that can be trusted. In five task domains, with up to seven author models, agents bring their programs to high scores. Yet when the environment changes, the checks they were told to write stay silent on half or more of the resulting failures in four domains. These failures can be detected and repaired: a monitor built from records of normal runs catches most of them in three domains, and the same agents usually repair them once called. The checks do not examine the recorded relations that reveal the failures, and the strongest agent writes checks that catch most of them once told that its checks are the only thing that calls it back. An unreported failure stays unrepaired, which limits what self-improvement is worth in autonomous operation. Evaluations of self-improvement should measure not only scores but also whether a system notices its own failures.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究递归自我改进 agent 在五个任务域中编写并修订程序，发现环境变化后其自写运行时检查会漏掉大量失败；基于正常运行记录构建的监控器能发现多数失败，且 agent 在被提示后通常可修复。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不涉及视觉或多模态推理，但其“系统能否察觉自身失败”的评测可能为 LVR 的自验证、停止决策与失败归因提供概念线索，可供核查其检查与监控设计能否映射到 latent 推理状态的核验。
